what: Pre-registration of the audit of two Lean proofs that integers multiply below n log n on a Turing machine. Committed on a local branch before the first pod-minute; the two intake specs beside it (corpus/lean-intake/intmul-gcmu, intmul-community) are part of it, and each carries its own amendments.

google-cmu.who: Piaoyang Cui, Yiming Liu, David P. Woodruff
google-cmu.linkedFrom: Google Research, "Advancing science & engineering with Antigravity's /teamwork feature", 2026-11-13

claims.source: OpenAI, "Integer multiplication below n log n", preprint of 2026-09-23 (result 109 of its math release), kappa = 2^-182; read only as the source both proofs point to. No verdict is given on it.

words.CERTIFIED: the Lean theorem proves exactly the pinned proposition, on propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice alone; Lean's kernel and nanoda (written independently, in Rust) both accept the proof; among the planted statements that reached the check every prediction is met, at least one changed statement is refused and at least one rewording is accepted; every planted defect is caught. It never says the mathematics is right beyond what the kernels checked, and nothing about practical speed.
words.REFUSED: a check did not give its positive answer; the reason is named (resources, a missing input, a mismatch). A build stopped by the time limit is REFUSED on resources.
words.reading: a comparison of a formal statement with a sentence of a paper is a reading, written out and kept apart from the verdicts.

questions.question: Does each headline theorem prove exactly its statement file, on three axioms, under two kernels?
questions.how: tools/lean-intake.js on one rented machine, both specs
questions.expected: google-cmu: CERTIFIED (its authors report the same checks accepted). community: no expectation; it has never been replayed outside its own CI, and its files use Lean's module system, which this tool has not met before.

questions.question: Does each statement say what its source says, in the source's machine model?
questions.how: two readings of each statement file against its paper, by readers who do not see each other's notes; the encodings evaluated on small pairs against an encoder of our own
questions.expected: faithful; the step from a multi-stack machine to a multitape machine rests on a classical simulation that neither proof formalizes.

questions.question: Are the two statements the same theorem?
questions.how: the three differences read on the scout (input encoding, form of the bound, finite alphabets); Lean where it is cheap
questions.expected: the two forms of the bound are equivalent at equal κ, and a proof of that closes; the encodings differ by a linear-time transducer, which may stay a written argument; a machine with an infinite work alphabet gains nothing, because every pushed symbol is the image of a finite state.

questions.question: Do our planted wrong statements and wrong proofs fail?
questions.expected: as each spec predicts; four statements carry no prediction ("kernel decides").

questions.question: Do the released programs compute products exactly, on inputs we choose?
questions.how: Python integers as the independent arithmetic, against the Python reference of Algorithm 1 and the C/GMP multiplier of the companion paper
questions.expected: exact on every input tried. Sizes above 10^8 bits are REFUSED on resources unless a smaller run predicts under an hour.

questions.question: In plain words, what does the theorem buy?
questions.how: exact arithmetic on the stated bound
questions.expected: the factor (log2 n)^(2^-46) reaches 2 only at n = 2^(2^(2^46)); C and N₀ are asserted to exist and are not given.

stopRules: One pod, 16 vCPU / 128 GB, US$ 0.88 an hour; the cap is US$ 15, approved by the operator on 2026-11-17; at 17 pod-hours the pod is deleted whatever is running.
A build still running after 8 hours is stopped and recorded REFUSED on resources.
If the google-cmu run does not reproduce what its authors report, the community run is stopped until the difference is read.
The encodings bridge gets one day; if it does not close it is published as a written argument and called one.
readBefore: Read on the scout, before this file: both READMEs, both statement files, the google-cmu Lean README and its authors' own replay record with nine planted controls (lean/replay), Mathlib's FinTM2 at 0df444a3, the community repository's theorem file and CI workflow, the C implementation's README. Nothing was built or run. The papers were not read.
